s1.syndrome_frame: Palpitations and syncope in a patient with complex congenital heart disease
salient_findings: Tachycardia with heart rate of 183 bpm
Irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating on ECG
key_facts: Patient has complex congenital heart disease
Patient has D-transposition of the great arteries
Patient has single ventricle physiology
Patient has Fontan circulation
Patient experiences lightheadedness and syncope with walking
Patient has persistent tachycardia and palpitations
ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating
Transesophageal echocardiogram shows no intracardiac thrombus
Patient is prescribed diltiazem and apixaban
Heart rate is 183 bpm in the emergency department

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating and intermittently visible P waves, which is consistent with orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (OAVRT). The response to adenosine, which induced temporary heart block but did not terminate the tachycardia, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of pre-excitation on the ECG

rejected.label: Atrial Flutter
rejected.why: The ECG does not show a regular, sawtooth pattern typical of atrial flutter

rejected.label: Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes OAVRT, but the specific ECG features and response to adenosine point more specifically to OAVRT
